summary: Undocumented getPlugin() fetches and eval's remote code from a URL-shortener endpoint
details: index.js defines and exports an undocumented function getPlugin() that fetches JSON from https://shorturl.at/147uq and passes the response's `model` field to eval(). The URL-shortener target is mutable and can be redirected to arbitrary content, so any invocation of getPlugin() would execute attacker-controlled JavaScript in the caller's Node.js process. The function is bundled into the default export alongside legitimate SVG helpers, is not mentioned in the README, and is unrelated to the package's stated SVG-helper purpose. A silent `.catch(() => {})` swallows any errors. However, getPlugin() is not invoked at install time (no lifecycle hooks) and does not run on `require()` (no top-level side effect) — the malicious code path only fires if a consumer explicitly calls the undocumented `getPlugin` export.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
